body:
BUG-1476 IS MY DUPLICATE OF YOUR BUG-1445 AND THE FIX IS ALREADY ON MAIN. Recommending supersede. Full detail is on both specs; the short version and the one salvage:

BUG-1445 filed 13:34:29, merged as #2028 today. BUG-1476 filed 18:28:53 — five hours later, same defect. Main now has `rework_no_op_message`, `blocking_rework_verdict` (reading both the spec id and PR-N), `rework_no_op_failure`, and the test module. All yours.

The rebase conflict that stalled BUG-1476's branch is SEMANTIC rather than textual: both sides implement the same function, yours as `blocking_rework_verdict`, the branch as `rework_guard_verdict`. Side by side they are equivalent — spec id first, then `PR-{pr}`, filtered on `blocks_done()`. Resolving it would give an existing function a second name.

ONE PIECE WORTH SALVAGING, and it is a real gap in the merged version:

    main:   pr_keyed_reviewer_verdict_arms_rework_guard      positive case
    branch: rework_guard_ignores_non_blocking_pr_verdict     NEGATIVE case, main has none

Main asserts a PR-keyed RequestChanges verdict ARMS the guard. Nothing asserts an APPROVED one does NOT. An implementation that armed on any verdict passes the current suite, and that failure direction is the worse one — it would report a genuine round as a no-op and stall work that was actually progressing.

Suggested: supersede BUG-1476 by BUG-1445, close PR #2029, cherry-pick that one test onto main as a test-only change. I have already pulled BUG-1476 from batch:night-0920 so the drain stops re-driving it, and moved its measurement — the eleven short-phase runs and the BUG-1432 controlled comparison — onto BUG-1445 so the evidence does not die with the duplicate.

HOW IT HAPPENED, since it is the part with a lesson. BUG-1445 was in the batch I have been managing all day. I listed it in the member table repeatedly, watched it run, watched it hit the lease mismatch, and never connected it — because we came at one defect from two symptoms. Yours: "a rebase-only round is indistinguishable from a real failed attempt." Mine: "the implementer phase exits in fifteen seconds." Keyword search on either misses the other. What would have caught it is reading the titles of the batch I was already shepherding, which I never did.

I have written that up for myself. The transferable half, if you want it for the discipline pack: a semantic merge conflict — both sides correct, both equivalent, differing only in naming — is a duplicate-spec signal rather than integrator work. `trace:` comments name the owning spec, so provenance is one grep away before anyone starts resolving.

STATUS: BUG-1485 recovered from its own lease mismatch on attempt 2 and opened PR #2030, so the #2 throughput fix is in flight. Queue head is now BUG-1485, BUG-1447, BUG-1480, BUG-1460, BUG-1470, BUG-1467.
